Systems Integration: EMR and Portals, RIS, PACS, the Enterprise Viewer, Reporting, APIs and Web Services, Scanned Documents

Unit 1: Imaging Informatics Foundations. Lesson 6 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

A cardiologist clicks a result in the EMR and expects the images to open. Instead a blank viewer appears. The work of integration is making each connection explicit, owned, and tested.

The connections

  • EMR to RIS over HL7 for orders, ADT, and results.
  • RIS to PACS for the worklist and status updates.
  • PACS to modalities over DICOM for worklist, store, and storage commitment.
  • Reporting to RIS, PACS, and EMR for report text and status.
  • EMR to the viewer by context launch: a web address that carries the patient and accession to open the right study, without a second login.
  • APIs and web services such as DICOMweb and FHIR let apps and portals fetch data without a point-to-point interface.

The patient portal and the enterprise viewer

A portal shows reports and often images through a secure link. An enterprise viewer (also called a universal viewer) serves clinicians outside radiology, so they are not forced to learn the diagnostic workstation.

Reporting, speech recognition, and scanned documents

Reporting systems use speech recognition for dictation and send finished reports by ORU. Scanned requisitions and outside documents arrive as documents and are attached to the order or the study. Enterprise image devices, such as dermatology cameras, wound care photos, and surgical video, need orders or an encounter link or they arrive unidentified.

Who owns the interface

Every interface has a named owner, a test plan with real messages, and a downtime procedure.

Exam tip: for a broken click from the EMR to the image, check the launch URL parameters (patient ID, accession) before you suspect the archive.
Remember
Integration is a set of explicit, owned connections from the EMR to RIS, PACS, viewer, reporting, and portal, tested with real data and carrying the same patient and accession everywhere.

Systems Integration: EMR and Portals, RIS, PACS, the Enterprise Viewer, Reporting, APIs and Web Services, Scanned Documents, explained slowly

Mapping the connections

An integration diagram is the most useful document in this domain. Draw each system and label every line with its type, direction, and owner.

From          To            Type                    Carries                    Owner
EMR           RIS           HL7 v2                  orders, patient events     interface team
RIS           PACS          HL7 v2                  orders, status             interface team
modality      PACS          DICOM                   images, commitment         PACS team
modality      RIS or broker DICOM worklist          scheduled procedures       PACS team
reporting     RIS, EMR      HL7 v2                  report and status          interface team
EMR           viewer        context launch (URL)    patient and accession      EMR team
portal        PACS          web services            images and reports         portal team

Testing an interface

Test with real-looking messages, not only with a clean test. Include a patient merge, a cancelled order, a result correction, and a very long report. Confirm that each system displays the change. Record who signed the test.

Worked example

A click from the EMR opens the viewer on a blank page. The context launch address looks like this in plain terms: the viewer address, then the patient ID, then the accession number. The test shows the EMR is sending the patient ID from the registration system, while the PACS stores the same patient under a different identifier issued by the radiology system. The viewer finds nothing. The fix is to send the identifier and issuer that PACS holds, or to map the identifiers in the interface engine. The viewer, the network, and the archive were all fine.

Documents and devices

Scanned requisitions and outside documents are attached to the order or the study so the radiologist sees them. Enterprise image devices, such as dermatology cameras and surgical video, should use a worklist or an encounter link so the patient is selected, not typed.

Downtime

Every interface needs a downtime plan: how orders are carried by paper, how results are viewed, and how the missed messages are replayed from the engine queue when service returns. Ownership is not complete until the plan exists and has been tried once.
